He played [[college basketball]] for the [[East Carolina Pirates men's basketball|East Carolina Pirates]] and the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]]. ==Early life== Hughes was born in [[Poughkeepsie, New York]] and grew up in [[Beacon, New York]]. He started playing basketball through the [[Catholic Youth Organization]] (CYO) and began playing on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) circuit for local coach, Kenney Dawson. Hughes became well-known in Beacon for his basketball ability, dominating games at Loopers Park.{{cite web |last1=Ditota |first1=Donna |title=Elijah Hughes, the 'Golden Child,' spins small-town promise into Syracuse basketball dream |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2019/08/elijah-hughes-the-golden-child-spins-small-town-promise-into-syracuse-basketball-dream.html |website=[[The Post-Standard]] |access-date=January 9, 2020 |date=August 8, 2019}} ==High school career== Following his eighth-grade basketball season, Hughes was called up to the [[varsity team]] at Beacon High School in [[Beacon, New York]]. Early in high school, he mainly played the [[point guard]] position despite his exceptional size. After two years at the school, Hughes transferred to [[John F. Kennedy Catholic High School (Somers, New York)|John F. Kennedy Catholic High School]] in [[Somers, New York]] with hopes of receiving more exposure.{{cite web |last1=Gutierrez |first1=Matthew |title=How Elijah Hughes went from an under-recruited mid-major prospect to Syracuse's budding star |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1333552/2019/10/30/how-elijah-hughes-went-from-an-under-recruited-mid-major-prospect-to-syracuses-budding-star/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=January 9, 2020 |date=October 30, 2019}} As a junior, Hughes led his team to a 26–2 record and runners-up finish at the [[Catholic High School Athletic Association]] (CHSAA) championship. Hughes was named first-team Class A All-State and CHSAA Class A [[most valuable player]] (MVP).{{cite web |last1=Waters |first1=Mike |title=Syracuse's Elijah Hughes says he's ready for starring role |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2019/10/syracuses-elijah-hughes-says-hes-ready-for-starring-role.html |website=[[The Post-Standard]] |access-date=January 9, 2020 |date=October 21, 2019}} He scored 42 points against [[Jamesville Dewitt High School]]. After the season, he committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[East Carolina Pirates men's basketball|East Carolina]]. However, he struggled academically, in part due to the long commute and the school's competitive academic environment. To help improve his grades and meet [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) requirements, Hughes transferred to [[South Kent School]], a [[boarding school]] in [[South Kent, Connecticut]], and later attended [[summer school]].{{cite web |last1=Manning |first1=Bobby |title=Elijah Hughes to fight for ACC scoring title as he leads Syracuse, inspires Beacon |url=https://www.nunesmagician.com/2019/11/5/20948746/elijah-hughe-syracuse-orange-virginia-acc-inspires-beacon-ncaa-speech-college-basketball-boeheim-acc |publisher=Troy Nunes Is An Absolute Magician |access-date=November 5, 2019 |date=November 5, 2019}} He became teammates with many other [[NCAA Division I]] prospects, including [[Tremont Waters]] and [[Myles Powell]]. Hughes was a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the No. 5 player in his state according to [[247Sports.com|247Sports]]. ==College career== Hughes began his collegiate career at [[East Carolina Pirates men's basketball|East Carolina]]. As a freshman, he averaged 7.8 and 2.3 rebounds in 27 games, missing seven games due to injury.{{cite web|url=https://www.nunesmagician.com/2017/5/10/15601522/east-carolina-transfer-elijah-hughes-will-visit-syracuse-beginning-on-wednesday-ecu-basketball/comment/428061789|title=East Carolina transfer Elijah Hughes will begin Syracuse visit today|first=Ben|last=Sigel|website=NunesMagician.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=May 10, 2017|access-date=January 11, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/east-carolina/LongFormArticle/ECU-basketball-transfers-departures-dismissals-Elijah-Hughes-Jeremy-Sheppard-Kentrell-Barkley-127960678/|title=Where are they now? Recent ECU hoops departures|first=Stephen|last=Igoe|website=247Sports.com|date=January 17, 2019|access-date=January 11, 2020}} The Pirates finished 15–18, and Hughes gained weight due to the injury. His season-high 19 points came against [[South Florida Bulls men's basketball|South Florida]] on December 28, 2016. Following the end of the season, Hughes announced that he would be leaving East Carolina.{{cite web|url=https://nsjonline.com/article/2017/04/ecu-loses-basketball-transfer/|title=Freshman Hughes leaving ECU basketball team|first=Brett|last=Friedlander|work=[[North State Journal]]|date=April 25, 2017|access-date=January 11, 2020}} Hughes decided to transfer to [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] over an offer from [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]].{{cite web|url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2017/05/east_carolina_transfer_elijah_hughes_commits_to_syracuse.html|title=East Carolina transfer Elijah Hughes commits to Syracuse|first=Mike|last=Waters|website=The Post-Standard|date=May 11, 2017|access-date=January 11, 2020}} After [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] a year due to NCAA transfer rules, during which he improved his strength and diet, Hughes was named a starter for the Orange going into his [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] sophomore season. He was the team's second leading scorer with 13.7 points per game while also averaging 4.3 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.2 steals per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.nunesmagician.com/2019/10/4/20898299/syracuse-basketball-preseason-player-profiles-elijah-hughes-orange-boeheim-ncaa-hoops-beacon-college|title=Syracuse basketball preseason player profiles: Elijah Hughes|first=Bobby|last=Manning|website=NunesMagician.com|publisher=SB Nation|date=October 4, 2019|access-date=January 11, 2020}} He took more three-pointers than any other teammate and made 36.9 percent of them. Hughes scored a career-high 25 points in the season-ending loss to [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]] in the NCAA tournament. Entering his junior season, Hughes was named to the watch list for the [[Julius Erving Award]], which honors the top collegiate [[small forward]].{{cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2019-10-16/college-basketball-awards-20-small-forwards-named-2020|title=College basketball awards: 20 small forwards named to 2020 Julius Erving Award preseason watch list|publisher=NCAA|date=October 16, 2019|access-date=October 23, 2019}} On February 11, 2020, Hughes left a game against [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]] early with a lower body injury.{{cite news |last1=Burrows |first1=Ben |title=Elijah Hughes leaves Syracuse basketball's game vs. NC State |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2020/02/elijah-hughes-leaves-syracuse-basketballs-game-vs-nc-state.html |access-date=February 11, 2020 |work=The Post-Standard |date=February 11, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Hughes was selected to the First Team All-ACC.{{cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/3/8/athlete-awards-2020-acc-mens-basketball-award-winners-announced.aspx|title=2020 ACC Men's Basketball Award Winners Announced|website=theacc.com|publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference|date=March 9, 2020|access-date=March 9, 2020}} As a junior, Hughes averaged 19 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 3.4 assists per game. After the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Weinstein |first1=Robbie |title=Syracuse star Elijah Hughes declares for 2020 NBA Draft |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Syracuse-Orange-star-Elijah-Hughes-declares-for-2020-NBA-Draft-145267950/ |access-date=March 21, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=March 21, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Utah Jazz (2020–2022)=== Hughes was selected with the 39th pick in the second round of the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. His draft rights were traded to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{Cite web|title=Elijah Hughes is Headed to the Utah Jazz|url=https://www.si.com/college/syracuse/basketball/elijah-hughes-selected-nba-draft|access-date=November 20, 2020|website=SI.com|date=November 18, 2020 |language=en}} On November 24, 2020, the [[Utah Jazz]] announced that they had signed with Hughes.{{cite web|title=Jazz sign Azubuike and Hughes|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-azubuike-and-hughes|date=November 24, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 24, 2020}} He was assigned to the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] of the [[NBA G League]] on February 15, 2021. ===Portland Trail Blazers (2022)=== On February 9,
